attempts.name: home-interior-v1
attempts.prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Create a finished chapter-specific derivative of reference image 1 for the same children's English-learning journey game. Preserve its soft painterly volume, rounded architecture, cream/coral/teal palette, warm upper-left daylight and gentle shadows. Reference image 2 is additional style guidance. REPLACE the spatial design with the chapter below; do not copy the colonnade, the residential street or their building placement.
EXACT native tall 1:3 canvas, preferably 724x2172, height exactly three times width, opaque RGB. ONE geographically continuous environment in consistent parallel oblique/isometric projection, not three independent pictures stacked vertically. The view has three contiguous square-length areas, but NO panel borders, horizontal seams, perspective restarts or repeated distant horizons. Preserve one traceable same-level walking surface from top to bottom. Roofs and side-room walls must not cut across that route.
Three unchanged full-body character/furniture groups will be rendered later; do NOT draw them. They have visible group height 36% of one square. Keep human-scale doors and furnishings compatible with these figures.
Reserve genuine FLAT SUPPORT SURFACES in global rectangles x23%-77%, y14%-23%, y47%-56%, and y80%-89%. Feet centers will be (50%,18.67%), (50%,52%), (50%,85.33%). These are real floor/paving, with no thresholds, stairs, rugs, grass, water, posts, furniture or abrupt dark shadows under feet. Keep center x30%-70% quiet below these positions for separately rendered stars and Lesson controls. Quiet natural floor, not blank circular pedestals. Support bands remain clear even where furniture is needed elsewhere.
Objects stay mainly along outer edges and in the rear/upper side bays. No people or animals. No writing, numbers, labels, signs, logos, UI, medals, stars, pins or watermarks. No floating islands, repeated round plazas or giant S bridges. No extra handheld lesson props or foreground furniture that would duplicate the unchanged character sprites.
CHAPTER: WARM HOME INTERIOR, Lesson25-30. Turn the outdoor reference into ONE roof-cutaway home with a broad continuous pale cream tiled hallway/floor, open kitchen, living and bedroom bays along its sides. Clearly interior: warm coral plaster, teal window frames, cream curtains, shallow wall moldings, restrained house plants. No outdoor road, garden balustrade or arcade. The same light tile scale continues between all three areas; side bays are open toward the viewer with no transverse partitions blocking the central floor.
UPPER AREA: kitchen details at the back/outer edges: one BLUE electric cooker on the LEFT and one WHITE refrigerator on the RIGHT; simple closed cupboards and a side sink. No central table, bottle or cup: the existing first sprite already contains a woman and a table with its only bottle/cup.
MIDDLE: a living-room side bay, television near a window with a small unmarked magazine stack above it; radio near the side doorway with a few unmarked books above. Keep all these outside the support band. No purple armchair and no extra table: the sprite already supplies its armchair.
LOWER: a calm bedroom side bay with one blue bed, wardrobe and open-window cue placed toward the outer/back margins. No broom, cleaning tools or additional figures. Keep the large shared foreground floor clear.
Use different side-bay arrangements, not three identical room elevations. The cutaway architecture must be physically coherent and the connecting floor continuous. Bright, warm, domestic and spacious, with the same illustration finish as the references.

CHAPTER: RIVER VALLEY WALK, Lesson31-36. A natural garden path connects a riverside bridge viewpoint and a village meadow. This is an open COUNTRY landscape, dominated by grass, mature trees and a turquoise river, with very little architecture. Do not reuse urban columns, dense houses or three formal garden terraces.
UPPER: a level, wide cream-stone garden path, a large leafy tree and flowering lawn borders at the sides. No people, cats or dogs.
MIDDLE: ONE broad STRAIGHT cream-stone BRIDGE DECK on the same walking route. The stream passes beneath it, visible at both outside edges; low parapets stay outside x20%-80%. Keep the ENTIRE middle support rectangle x23%-77%, global y47%-56% as flat bridge paving so the family can stand on the bridge. No water under the foot zone. One tiny unoccupied boat can be far out on the river to the side. NO aircraft: the accepted family sprite already includes its single aeroplane.
LOWER: the same route reaches a green village bank, with a small coral-roof cottage and modest school facade well off to a distant side, a wooden gate and meadow flowers. No extra album or photo objects; the existing pair holds the only album.
Use one continuous route with physically supported banks and bridge, consistent projection and scale. No cliff-like isolated islands, repeated arched water gardens, seams or new horizon between zones. Human standing areas are always paved, not grass or water. Airy countryside, restrained planting and warm sunshine.

CHAPTER: HANDCRAFT COURTYARD, Lesson37-42. A single continuous warm PALE TERRACOTTA BRICK courtyard connects a small carpentry shed, a home display alcove and a pantry/back porch. Strong craft identity: timber roof beams, simple brick walls, restrained teal doors, stacked raw timber at an OUTER edge. Mostly one open courtyard, not three room panels. Different from both the cream-tiled home interior and the green riverside.
UPPER: an open carpentry shed to one side with an EMPTY pegboard and neatly stored raw planks. No hammer, paint can, bookcase or workbench in the environment: the first sprite already contains George, Dan, the only wooden bookcase and pink paint can.
MIDDLE: a quiet wall alcove/window and built-in planting bed at the side, open brick paving in the middle. No flower-filled vase or shelf unit: both are already in the sprite. Avoid decorative vases that could look like a second lesson vase.
LOWER: a welcoming back porch and plain closed pantry cabinets at the side, perhaps a small gate. No chair, shopping bag, bread, milk or cheese: the existing sprite contains the exact shopping scene.
The same lightly textured brick surface runs through all three support regions; low-contrast joints and subtle warm sunlight, no steps or structural posts across the standing bands. Craft details sit outside the central human/furniture area. Finished sunny storybook game environment, not a shop advertisement or construction site.

CHAPTER: TEA AND LETTERS SUNROOM, Lesson43-48. A warm domestic conservatory/guest-room gallery with a continuous LIGHT HONEY WOOD floor. Tall teal-framed glass windows, a few pale coral wall sections and restrained climbing greenery at the OUTER edges make this airy glass-and-wood place distinct from the tiled home, river valley and brick workshop. Cutaway roof view, one continuous wide interior floor, no repeated street facades or separate panels.
UPPER: a tea-preparation alcove with simple EMPTY cupboards toward the side. No tea trolley, teapot, kettle, tea packet or cups: the first sprite already supplies its exact trolley and tea objects.
MIDDLE: a quiet writing/office nook with empty pigeonholes and a closed cabinet at the outer side, window light on the wood floor. No letter, typewriter, small pedestal table or new people: the second sprite supplies those.
LOWER: a welcoming conversation area opening through a side arch toward a tiny garden terrace. A SINGLE small plain milk jug may rest on a narrow side console FAR to the right, clearly outside the support zone. No cups, biscuits or pouring: the two women in the existing sprite already hold the only coffee cup and biscuit.
The wood floor remains flat, quiet and uninterrupted through all support bands, with no rugs or thresholds. Use gentle sunlight through the glazing, never harsh stripe shadows across the characters' feet or label bands. Warm private hospitality rather than a commercial cafe, no menus or signs. Same soft-volume painterly finish as the reference.
